html:
Shia Islam is the second largest branch of Islam, after Sunni Islam. Its followers hold that the leadership of the community after Muhammad belonged to his cousin and son-in-law Ali and then to Ali's descendants, the imams.

The name comes from "shiat Ali", the party of Ali. The split began as a political dispute over who should lead after the prophet's death in 632 (see Succession to Muhammad). Most Muslims accepted the first caliph, Abu Bakr; Ali's supporters felt he had been passed over. The quarrel hardened during the First Fitna, Ali's murder in 661 and the killing of his son Husayn at the Battle of Karbala in 680, which Shia Muslims mourn each year at Ashura.

Over centuries, differences in law, ritual and belief grew. Shia Muslims are a majority today in Iran, Iraq and Bahrain, and large minorities live in many other countries.
